findings.evidence: Lines 338/355/368 define the only `_succ`-family lemmas in the file; `mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecificLimits/Basic.lean:237` etc. use `pow_succ'` only alongside the existing `pow_succ`.
findings.fix: Drop the primes (`mul_deriv_sphericalBesselJ_succ`, `hasDerivAt_sphericalBesselJ_succ`, `deriv_sphericalBesselJ_succ`) — the statements are about `sphericalBesselJ (l + 1)`, so `_succ` is accurate and unused — or give a suffix naming the content; update the module docstring at lines 57 and 59 and the use at line 414.
findings.issue: `mul_deriv_sphericalBesselJ_succ'` (line 338), `hasDerivAt_sphericalBesselJ_succ'` (line 355) and `deriv_sphericalBesselJ_succ'` (line 368) carry a prime, but no unprimed `..._succ` declaration exists in the PR (grep for `succ'` in the file returns only these three plus their uses). In Mathlib a prime marks a variant of a same-named lemma (`pow_succ'`/`pow_succ`, `sum_range_succ'`/`sum_range_succ`), so the prime here points at nothing and gives the consumer no way to tell the order-lowering relation from `hasDerivAt_sphericalBesselJ (l+1)`.

findings.evidence: Line 87 `noncomputable def reducedSphericalBesselJ`; the References block (lines 68-72) lists only A&S §10.1 and DLMF §§10.47/10.49(ii)/10.51/10.52, none of which defines a "reduced" spherical Bessel function.
findings.fix: Rename to something that does not claim standard terminology, e.g. `rayleighIterate` / `sphericalBesselJRayleigh` (matching DLMF §10.49(ii), already cited), or at minimum state in the definition docstring that "reduced" here means `j_l(x) / x ^ l` and not `x * j_l(x)`.
findings.issue: `reducedSphericalBesselJ` (and its docstrings, lines 82, 90, 98, 102, 129-152, 184) names `j_l(x)/x^l` "the reduced spherical Bessel function". That term is not defined in either source the module cites (A&S §10.1, DLMF §§10.47, 10.49(ii), 10.51, 10.52), while "reduced" for spherical Bessel functions conventionally denotes `x * j_l(x)` (the Riccati–Bessel function / reduced radial function) — the reciprocal modification. A consumer grepping for `reducedSphericalBessel` gets the opposite object from the one the term usually names.

summary: Two naming issues: a trio of primed `_succ'` lemmas whose unprimed counterparts do not exist, and the `reducedSphericalBesselJ` name, which claims terminology that conventionally denotes a different object. Everything else (namespaces, iff suffixes, dot-notation placement, local notation) follows Mathlib precedent.
